usageNotes: Use this to discard all pending (unapplied) SDN changes and revert the SDN configuration back to its last committed state. This is a synchronous operation that returns null on success, not a UPID task. If you hold the global SDN lock (e.g., from a failed apply attempt), pass the lock token via `lock-token` and set `release-lock` to true so the lock is cleared in a single call.

examples.summary: Rollback pending SDN changes and release a held lock in one call

destructiveReason: Permanently discards all pending SDN configuration changes that have not yet been applied, making them unrecoverable.
tips: The SDN.Allocate privilege on /sdn is required; ensure your API token or user has this permission.
If no lock is held, both lock-token and release-lock can be omitted — the endpoint will still rollback pending changes.
After rollback, verify the current committed state with GET /cluster/sdn before making new changes.
This is commonly used as a recovery step when a prior apply (POST /cluster/sdn) failed and left the configuration in a dirty state.
